units.passage: Be cautious when clicking links, and make sure you have good antivirus protection.
units.why: Users should be 'cautious when clicking links' and keep antivirus; security awareness (P75).
units.fit_note: Concerns links in AI output and antivirus, not phishing explicitly.

units.passage: Gen AI has made it easier for malicious actors to create sophisticated scams, and individuals using AI technology must consider privacy risks, exposure of intellectual property, and the potential threat of data breaches utilizing information provided to Gen AI software.
units.why: "Gen AI has made it easier for malicious actors to create sophisticated scams" is a security-awareness warning (P75) and tells users to "consider privacy risks"; P75 fits better than P50 because the threat is scams.

units.passage: Generative AI tools also make it easier for malicious actors to create sophisticated scams at a far greater scale.
units.why: "make it easier for malicious actors to create sophisticated scams" is a security-awareness warning, so P75; informs.

units.passage: Generative AI has made it easier for malicious actors to create sophisticated phishing emails and to create video or audio intended to convincingly mimic a person’s voice or physical appearance without their consent
units.why: "Generative AI has made it easier for malicious actors to create sophisticated phishing emails and ... deepfakes" is a security-awareness warning, so P75; informs.

units.passage: Exercise caution when utilizing AI tools, particularly with personal information. Be vigilant against potential phishing schemes that may exploit passwords, emails, and other sensitive information. Maintain a heightened awareness of security risks.
units.why: 'Be vigilant against potential phishing schemes that may exploit passwords, emails, and other sensitive information' warns users about AI-enabled phishing while they use AI tools, so P75, should, during-work.

units.passage: Employees must use extreme caution when opening e-mail attachments received from unknown senders, which may contain viruses, e-mail bombs, or Trojan horse code and/or may be considered “phishing”.
units.why: "Employees must use extreme caution when opening e-mail attachments received from unknown senders" is a phishing warning in an AI guideline, P75, must.
units.fit_note: Concerns email attachments generally, not AI-crafted phishing specifically.

units.passage: Continue to follow cybersecurity best practices and report any suspicious communications to ET&S Client Services
units.why: Under 'Be Vigilant Against AI-Enabled Phishing', users should 'report any suspicious communications'; AI phishing awareness (P75).

units.passage: NEVER share your Banner ID or username and password with AI tools, and always be aware of phishing schemes.
units.why: 'always be aware of phishing schemes' in the same sentence tells users to watch for phishing (P75).

units.passage: Be extra vigilant about potential phishing attacks.
units.why: "Be extra vigilant about potential phishing attacks. Generative AI is rapidly changing the phishing landscape" is AI-enabled phishing awareness, so P75.

units.passage: Report any questionable emails to University Information Technology (UIT) by clicking the Phish Notify button in Outlook/O365 or submitting a helpdesk ticket.
units.why: "Report any questionable emails to University Information Technology (UIT)" gives a channel for suspicious messages. P75 covers phishing reporting, nearest type; it is a separate action from staying vigilant.

units.passage: When using AI to write computer code or when creating new technology that leverages AI it is important to be aware of the new kinds of cyberattacks that are being used against AI users. Review the Office of Information Security guidance on these risks or consult with the Office of Information Security if in doubt.
units.why: Tells users writing code with AI to be aware of "new kinds of cyberattacks that are being used against AI users" and to consult security; closest is P75 (security threats) but this is about attacks on AI users and AI-built tech, not AI-enabled phishing.
units.fit_note: Covers attacks aimed at users of AI and AI-built code, not AI-crafted phishing. | Concerns cyberattacks on users of AI-written code and AI-based technology, not AI-crafted phishing; also tells users to consult the security office.

units.passage: Be aware that GenAI technologies can be exploited for sophisticated phishing scams or cybersecurity threats
units.policy: Be aware that GenAI technologies can be exploited for sophisticated phishing scams or cybersecurity threats.
units.why: 'Be aware that GenAI technologies can be exploited for sophisticated phishing scams' is security awareness, P75.

units.passage: Constantly scrutinize GenAI-generated messages and links for authenticity and report any suspicious activity to the IT Security Office - security@sdsu.edu
units.policy: Constantly scrutinize GenAI-generated messages and links for authenticity and report any suspicious activity to the IT Security Office.
units.why: 'scrutinize GenAI-generated messages and links ... and report any suspicious activity' to IT Security is a duty to check and report, P75.

units.passage: Generative AI has made it easier for bad actors to create scams on a larger scale.
units.why: "Generative AI has made it easier for bad actors to create scams on a larger scale" warns of AI-enabled phishing, so P75.

units.passage: The Visual Media Policy (Policy 8205) must be reviewed to consider the growing challenges
units.policy: The Visual Media Policy (Policy 8205) must be reviewed to consider the growing challenges of AI-generated imagery and deepfake technology.
units.why: The Visual Media Policy 'must be reviewed to consider the growing challenges of AI-generated imagery and deepfake technology'; the deepfake concern under P75 (AI-enabled threats), with a fit note since it is a policy review.
units.fit_note: A commitment to review a policy for deepfakes, not guidance to users on spotting threats.
